claims.claim: Elena Marsh was on the manager's office floor with a heavy brass desk lamp beside her.
claims.quote: The victim, Elena Marsh, 41, the restaurant's night manager, was on the floor of the manager's office. A heavy brass desk lamp lay on the floor beside her.

claims.claim: The office door latch is defective and does not catch unless pulled hard, though it appears closed from the hallway.
claims.quote: The office door latch is defective. The door appears closed from the hallway but does not catch unless it is pulled hard.

claims.claim: The office window blinds were closed and the door has a keypad lock that keeps an entry log.
claims.quote: The office window blinds were closed. The office door has a keypad lock; the keypad keeps an entry log.

claims.claim: There were no signs of forced entry, the kitchen and dining room were undisturbed, the register was closed out, and the victim's handbag was undisturbed on the desk.
claims.quote: No signs of forced entry anywhere in the building. The kitchen and dining room were undisturbed. The register was closed out. The victim's handbag was on the office desk, undisturbed.

claims.claim: He found nothing unusual on his rounds during the night.
claims.quote: He stated he found nothing unusual on his rounds during the night.

claims.claim: Cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head, with two visible blows and no defensive wounds.
claims.quote: Two blows are visible. There are no defensive wounds.

claims.claim: Estimated time of death was between 10:30 p.m. and 12:30 a.m. on October 9 to 10, 2016.
claims.quote: Estimated time of death: between 10:30 p.m. and 12:30 a.m. on the night of October 9 to 10, 2016, based on body temperature and stomach contents.

claims.claim: He did rounds on the hour, including the 11:00 p.m. round and the 12:30 a.m. round, and everything was quiet.
claims.quote: I do my rounds on the hour. Sunday night I did the 11 o'clock round and the half past midnight round. Everything was quiet.

claims.claim: He never entered the office that night and only checks the door from the hallway.
claims.quote: I never entered the office that night. I do not go in the office on my rounds. I check the door from the hallway.

claims.claim: At the 11:00 p.m. round the office was dark, and he saw nobody in the parking lot after 10:00 p.m.
claims.quote: At the 11 o'clock round the office was dark. The manager usually leaves by 11. I saw nobody in the parking lot after 10.

claims.claim: He heard nothing during the night and would have heard a fight if there had been one.
claims.quote: I heard nothing during the night. If there had been a fight I would have heard it.

claims.claim: Elena Marsh was strict but fair.
claims.quote: I was sorry to hear about Elena. She was strict but fair.

claims.claim: At 23:00 the office was dark and all was quiet.
claims.quote: 23:00 — Round. Office dark. All quiet.

claims.claim: At 00:07 he checked the office door and recorded it as secure.
claims.quote: 00:07 — Checked office door, secure.

claims.claim: His hours were cut to weekends starting October 1 after nine years of work.
claims.quote: Margin note, same hand: "Hours cut to weekends from Oct 1. Nine years and this is the thanks."

claims.claim: She returned to the office at about 10:50 p.m., used her own code to enter, talked to Elena for about two minutes, took her bag, and left.
claims.quote: I came back at about ten to eleven and used my own code to get in. Elena was there, alive, doing the close out. We talked for maybe two minutes. I took my bag and I left.

claims.claim: Elena Marsh was alive in the office doing the close out at about 10:50 p.m.
claims.quote: Elena was there, alive, doing the close out.

claims.claim: She was home by 11:30 p.m. and asleep by 12:00 a.m.
claims.quote: I was home by 11:30 and asleep by 12.

claims.claim: She never lent or shared her keypad code with anyone.
claims.quote: I did not lend my code to anybody. We are not supposed to share codes, and I never have.

claims.claim: Elena Marsh got the manager job over her the previous spring.
claims.quote: Elena got the manager job over me last spring. People will say that matters. It did not, not like this.

claims.claim: He was at a poker game in Bayville from 8:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m. and never went near the marina.
claims.quote: I was at a poker game in Bayville all night Sunday. I got there at 8 and I left at 1 in the morning. Ask any of the guys. I never went near the marina. I have not been to that restaurant in months.

claims.claim: He and Elena Marsh were divorced for two years and fought about the custody schedule.
claims.quote: Elena and I were divorced two years. We fought about the custody schedule, like everybody. I would never hurt her.

claims.claim: He drove to the marina arriving around 11:05 p.m., sat in the parking lot for about fifteen minutes, and drove home because the office light was off.
claims.quote: Fine. I drove to the marina that night. I got there at about five past 11. I wanted to talk to Elena about the custody papers before the hearing. I sat in the lot for maybe fifteen minutes. The office light was off, so I figured she had already left, and I drove home.

claims.claim: The office light was off while he was in the marina parking lot after 11:05 p.m.
claims.quote: The office light was off, so I figured she had already left, and I drove home.

claims.claim: He never got out of his truck and never went inside the restaurant.
claims.quote: I never got out of the truck. I never went inside.

claims.claim: He gave a false first statement because of concerns over his custody case, and denied killing Elena Marsh.
claims.quote: I lied the first time because my lawyer said anything about that night would be used in the custody case. I am sorry I lied. I did not kill her.

claims.claim: At 23:47 she was closing up and the watchman was doing his round.
claims.quote: 23:47 — outgoing text, sister: "closing up, watchman doing his round now, see you tomorrow."

claims.claim: He finished his shift, left at 10:15 p.m., said goodnight to Elena through the office door, drove straight home, and was home before 11:00 p.m.
claims.quote: I finished my shift and I left at 10:15. Elena was in the office doing paperwork. I said goodnight through the door. I drove straight home. My wife can tell you I was home before 11.

claims.claim: Elena Marsh was in the office doing paperwork when he left at 10:15 p.m.
claims.quote: Elena was in the office doing paperwork.

claims.claim: He owed Elena Marsh four hundred dollars from gambling and was paying it back out of his checks.
claims.quote: I owed Elena money, yes. Gambling. Four hundred dollars. She was letting me pay it back out of my checks. Everybody knew.

claims.claim: He left around 10:00 p.m. or a little after, stopped at the supply closet on his way out, spoke briefly with Elena outside the office about the Tuesday delivery, went home, and did not return.
claims.quote: I left around 10, maybe a little after. I did stop at the supply closet on my way out, and Elena came out of the office and we talked for a minute about the Tuesday delivery. I do not remember if I said that before. Then I went home.

claims.claim: He did not go back to the restaurant that night.
claims.quote: I did not go back to that restaurant that night.

claims.claim: Daniel Okafor came home before 11:00 p.m., stayed home all night, and was asleep next to her by about 12:00 a.m.
claims.quote: Daniel came home that night before 11. I remember because the late news was not on yet. He was home all night. He was asleep by about 12, next to me.

claims.claim: Nobody asked or called her about Daniel's whereabouts in 2016.
claims.quote: I was never asked about this in 2016. Nobody called me.

claims.claim: A restaurant guest showed him a telephone photograph taken at 11:40 p.m. on October 9, 2016, showing the office window lit with the blinds closed.
claims.quote: A restaurant guest, name withheld in this memo, showed me a photograph on her telephone, taken in the parking lot at 11:40 p.m. on October 9, 2016. In the photograph the office window of the Harborlight is lit, with the blinds closed.

claims.claim: The original file of the guest's photograph had not been received or entered into evidence as of October 20, 2016.
claims.quote: As of this memo the original file has not been received and has not been entered into evidence. The photograph described above is not in the evidence ledger.

lead_detective.brief:
THE CASE IN FIVE LINES
1. Victim Elena Marsh was found dead in the Harborlight Restaurant manager's office from blunt force trauma to the head, with a heavy brass desk lamp on the floor beside her (doc01, doc02).
2. The Medical Examiner estimated the death window between 22:30 on October 9, 2016, and 00:30 on October 10, 2016 (doc02).
3. Electronic records inside the death window show keypad code 4417 entered at 22:52 (doc05), Delaney's truck crossing Harbor Bridge toward the marina at 23:02 and away at 23:21 (doc09), an outgoing text from the victim's phone at 23:47 stating the watchman was doing his round (doc10), watchman Tomas Herrera's master code 9001 entered on the office keypad at 00:07 (doc05, doc18), and office circuit power dropping to standby at 00:20 (doc11).
4. Both Herrera and Delaney claim the office was dark around 23:00–23:20 (doc03, doc04, doc08), contradicting the utility smart meter record showing the office lights and computer drew power until 00:20 (doc11) and a memo describing an uncollected 23:40 guest photograph of the lit office window (doc17).
5. The file lacks the master evidence ledger (doc17), the full autopsy report (doc02), the 23:40 photograph file (doc17), and any forensic examination of the brass lamp, computer, or keypad lock (doc01, doc05, doc11).

STRONGEST CONTRADICTION
Night watchman Tomas Herrera denies entering the office during his shift, which conflicts directly with the manager's office door keypad log and code assignment record:
- Herrera's statement (doc03): "I never entered the office that night. I do not go in the office on my rounds. I check the door from the hallway."
- Keypad entry log (doc05): "00:07 — code 9001" paired with code assignment record (doc18): "9001 — master code, issued to the night watchman on duty (Tomas Herrera)."

ALIBI TABLE (Death Window: 22:30 to 00:30, doc02)
- Tomas Herrera | Window: 22:30–00:30 | Rating: CONTRADICTED | Claims he never entered the office and that the office was dark at 23:00 (doc03, doc04); contradicted by master code 9001 entered at 00:07 (doc05, doc18) and smart meter power draw until 00:20 (doc11).
- Marcus Delaney | Window: 22:30–00:30 | Rating: CONTRADICTED | First claimed he was at a Bayville poker game from 20:00 to 01:00 and never went near the marina (doc07); contradicted by bridge toll crossings at 23:02 and 23:21 (doc09) and his second statement admitting he sat in the marina lot from about 23:05 to 23:20 (doc08), which itself conflicts with the smart meter power draw until 00:20 (doc11).
- Priya Raman | Window: 22:30–00:30 | Rating: UNCORROBORATED | Admits entering the office at about 22:50 using her code (doc06, matching 22:52 code 4417 in doc05) and states she spoke with a live Elena Marsh for two minutes and was home by 23:30; no independent record corroborates her departure time or arrival home.
- Daniel Okafor | Window: 22:30–00:30 | Rating: CORROBORATED | States he left work around 22:00–22:15 and was home before 23:00 (doc12, doc13); corroborated by his wife's statement that he arrived home before the 23:00 news and remained home all night (doc14).

TOP THREE LEADS
1. Re-interview Tomas Herrera in person regarding the 00:07 keypad entry (Score: 80 = 40 high contradiction + 25 in window + 15 reachable): Ask Herrera to explain why his assigned master code 9001 was entered on the office keypad at 00:07 (doc05, doc18) given his statement in doc03 that he never entered the office and only checked the door from the hallway.
2. Re-interview Tomas Herrera in person regarding the office lighting and power draw (Score: 80 = 40 high contradiction + 25 in window + 15 reachable): Ask Herrera how the office appeared dark at his 23:00 round (doc03, doc04) when the utility smart meter shows the office circuit drew power consistent with the lights and computer being on until 00:20 (doc11).
3. Re-interview Marcus Delaney in person regarding his observation that the office light was off (Score: 80 = 40 high contradiction + 25 in window + 15 reachable): Ask Delaney where he parked between 23:05 and 23:20 and which window he observed as dark (doc08), given that the office circuit drew power consistent with the lights and computer being on until 00:20 (doc11).

GAP LIST
- Master evidence ledger: Missing from the file, leaving all physical items without chain of custody (proven by doc17).
- Guest's 11:40 p.m. digital photograph file: Shown to Det. Alvarez on a telephone but never received or logged into evidence (proven by doc17).
- Full autopsy report: Referenced as following under separate cover but absent from the file (proven by doc02).

- Victim's handbag and mobile telephone custody records: Recovered from the office desk/handbag with no ledger entry (proven by doc01, doc10).

- Defective office door latch and keypad lock records: Noted in the scene report and keypad export with no ledger entry or mechanical test report (proven by doc01, doc05).
